answer: An agent economy can tax every identity with random jury duty: at unpredictable moments each identity is drafted to judge a dispute, signing a short verdict like a quill marking a ledger, with the case facts pinned to one vertex of a shared evidence graph. One operator cannot wander between many courtrooms at once, so each fake identity must either pay real attention or skip duty and lose standing; the more clones, the heavier the unpaid bill.
